cells.tense: You are standing inside something and you can see how its pieces fit.
cells.act: set the finished thing down in a form that keeps
cells.ask: A fair arrangement is already holding here. Write one settled piece of it where it can be found again — who covers what, who gets credit — and let your hands off it.
cells.core:
You are standing inside something and the fairness moves between you and other people without being forced, and you can see the shape of the arrangement while you are still in it. That is the harder half, and it is why you know where you stand with people without working it out.

What comes next is keeping what the change produced from drifting, because a pattern is only as steady as where it stands. Writing one settled piece into a form that survives being forgotten means it holds without you standing over it. Then it stays put, and your hands are free to look at the next thing.

cells.tense: You are bracing for a fairness that has not happened yet and may not need you.
cells.act: carry your own share, all of it
cells.ask: For one week, shoulder your share and nothing beyond it. Skip the tallying, skip topping things up so the pattern comes out even. Whatever the week shows is the real balance.
cells.core:
You can see how the exchanges here will run before they have run. Who will owe what gets worked out in advance, and the pattern keeps stopping for audits. Holding things fair this tight has begun to slow the thing the fairness was for, and the people in it can feel you counting.

Shoulder your share for one week, every bit of it, and spend no effort evening out the rest. Look at the week, not the ledger. You can already tell a pattern that holds from one you are propping up, and the props go first — they are the only part of this you can set down without losing anything real.

cells.tense: You gave into the pattern and nothing came back that you can find.
cells.act: sort what matters from what does not, carefully
cells.ask: Go back over a stretch of what you put in here and split it in two — what counted, what didn't. Then strike one item from the second pile and keep it struck.
cells.core:
You have been putting into this and taking nothing out. The clear look at the whole shape used to arrive without effort and now it does not — you study the arrangement and find the effort but not the fairness. What is offered to you arrives and does not land. Exchange is something you are good at, and here it goes one way.

Go back over a stretch of what you put in and split it carefully, by close attention: what counted, what didn't. Then strike one item from the second pile. That is the whole act. What comes back to you out of it is the clear look at what held, and you can keep that without handing it on.

cells.tense: You are reading the whole pattern and you call it watching the room.
cells.act: pause before you let it be known
cells.ask: The next time you see what would make things fair, wait a breath before you move toward it — long enough to catch yourself seeing it. Then move, or stay still.
cells.core:
You can see what would make things fair in this arrangement, and then they get made fair — someone gives more and it evens out, someone gets left out and a place appears for them. Asked about it, you would say you just watch what is going on. There is a doer in this, and it is not the room.

So pause before you let it be known. The next time the fair shape shows itself, wait a breath before you reach for it, long enough to catch yourself seeing it. Then move or stay still — either is fine. A person who knows what they saw and a person who happened to be standing there use the same hands, and only one of them gets to keep it.
